headline: Price of 12kg LPG jumps by Tk 252 amid supply crunch
summary: The Bangladesh Energy Regulatory Commission (BERC) has raised the price of a 12kg LPG cylinder to Tk 1,837, following a rise in international market prices.
details: The price of a 12kg LPG cylinder has increased by Tk 252, with the Bangladesh Energy Regulatory Commission (BERC) setting the new rate at Tk 1,837, up from Tk 1,585.
The revised rate took effect from 6:00pm today. Prices for cylinders between 5.5kg and 45kg have also increased proportionately, set at Tk 153.06 per kg.
Additionally, the price of autogas used for vehicles has been raised to Tk 84.62 per litre, up from the previous rate of Tk 73.09.
BERC stated that the adjustment was made in line with higher international LPG prices, as the regulator reviews rates monthly based on the global market.
The hike comes during a period where consumers in several areas are already struggling to find LPG despite paying prices higher than the government-fixed rate.
Reports indicate that retailers in some areas have been selling 12kg cylinders for Tk 2,200 to Tk 2,500, significantly exceeding the new official rate.
This follows a supply disruption that had already pushed retail prices up; last month, some consumers paid Tk 400-600 more than the regulated price.

headline: 1,125 dead as measles outbreak spreads across Bangladesh
summary: The combined toll of confirmed and suspected measles cases has reached 1,125 deaths this year, according to the DGHS.
details: Three more people died from suspected measles in the last 24 hours, with two deaths in Dhaka Division and one in Rangpur.
According to the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS), the total number of deaths with suspected measles symptoms this year has reached 1,023.
An additional 102 people have died after being confirmed to have measles, bringing the combined death toll to 1,125.
Dhaka Division has recorded the highest number of fatalities with 465 deaths, followed by Sylhet with 179, Rajshahi with 93, and Chattogram with 86.
In the last 24 hours alone, 1,218 patients with measles symptoms sought treatment, and 1,122 were admitted to hospitals nationwide.
The total number of hospital admissions for suspected measles symptoms this year has reached 174,149, with 166,908 patients having recovered and been discharged.
The DGHS reports that 196,418 people have shown suspected measles symptoms, and 21,748 of these cases have been confirmed as measles.
Authorities noted that not all patients undergo testing, meaning the exact number of confirmed cases may be higher than recorded figures.
